subject: Logic
title: Probabilistic Forecasting
description: A micro-lesson that makes Probabilistic Forecasting usable.

hook.text: "Will it rain?" is the wrong question. "What's the 70% rain zone?" is how forecasters actually think.

buildup.text: Probabilistic forecasts express confidence as a range, not a single prediction.

discovery.text: Superforecasters—the best predictors alive—think in precise percentages: 73%, not "probably."

twist.text: A 70% forecast that's wrong 30% of the time isn't bad—it's perfectly calibrated.

climax.text: The best forecasters update constantly, think in ranges, and track their accuracy over time.

punchline.text: Good forecasts are ranges, not bets.

quiz.question: What distinguishes a probabilistic forecast from a regular prediction?
options: It expresses confidence as a probability range
